title: Essentially smooth local DVR extensions have ramification index one
statement: Let $D$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $\pi$ generate its maximal ideal, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $k=D/(\pi)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ be smooth [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $x$ lie over the closed point of $S$. Suppose $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a discrete valuation ring and the induced map $D\to A$ is local and injective. Here local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Then $\pi A=\mathfrak m_A$, and the residue-field extension $\kappa(x)/k$ [def-weil-residue-field] is separably generated: it admits a finite transcendence basis over which it is finite separable. In particular $\kappa(x)\otimes_k k'$ is reduced for every field extension $k'/k$. Equivalently, this is a ramification-one extension in the terminology that requires both a common uniformizer and a separable residue-field extension. No excellence, completeness, or perfection of $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $s=(\pi)$ and $Y=X_s$, and let $y$ be its point over $x$. The fibre-stalk quotient theorem gives $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\cong A/\pi A$, compatibly with $k=D/(\pi)$; here $D_{(\pi)}=D$, since every element outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $D$ is already a unit. Smoothness gives geometrically reduced fibres: by definition $Y_\Omega=Y\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is reduced for every separably closed extension $\Omega/k$. Claim (*): for every field extension $L/k$ and every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C'\subseteq Y$, $C'\otimes_kL$ is reduced. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $L$; it is algebraically closed, hence separably closed (a separable polynomial splits by extracting roots one at a time). $\operatorname{Spec}(C'\otimes_k\Omega)=\operatorname{Spec}C'\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the pullback of the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}C'\hookrightarrow Y$ along $Y_\Omega\to Y$, so it is open in $Y_\Omega$ and $C'\otimes_k\Omega$ is reduced by the section characterization. For a $k$-basis $(e_j)$ of $C'$, $C'\otimes_kL=\bigoplus_jLe_j\subseteq\bigoplus_j\Omega e_j=C'\otimes_k\Omega$, so $C'\otimes_kL$ is a subring of a reduced ring, hence reduced. Localization fact: a localization of a reduced ring is reduced, since $(a/s)^N=0$ gives some denominator $v$ with $va^N=0$, whence $(va)^N=0$, $va=0$ and $a/s=0$. With $L=k$, every affine open ring of $Y$ is reduced, and every stalk of $Y$ is a localization of one by the affine stalk localization theorem. Thus $A/\pi A\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is reduced.

source.place: Schemes Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre); Morphisms Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); Varieties Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: Choose a generator $t\ne0$ of $\mathfrak m_A$. The DVR factorization theorem gives $\pi=ut^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\ge0$. Injectivity ensures $\pi\ne0$ in $A$, and locality gives $\pi\in\mathfrak m_A$, so $e\ge1$. If $e\ge2$, the class of $t$ in $A/\pi A$ is nilpotent since $t^e=u^{-1}\pi$. It is nonzero: $t=\pi a=ut^ea$ would give $1=ut^{e-1}a$ after cancellation in the domain $A$, making the nonunit $t$ a unit. This contradicts Step 1. Thus $e=1$, $\pi A=tA=\mathfrak m_A$, and the quotient identification in Step 1 identifies $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with $F=\kappa(x)$ as a $k$-algebra.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; elementary nilpotent calculation in the quotient.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$ on which $B$ is finitely presented over $D$; this is possible by smoothness and the definition of local finite presentation. The affine base neighbourhood contains the closed point of the local scheme $\operatorname{Spec}D$, so it is all of $\operatorname{Spec}D$: a basic open containing that point is defined by a unit. The affine fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C=B\otimes_Dk=B/\pi B$. It is an open neighbourhood of $y$ in $Y$: it is the pullback of the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow X$. It is finitely presented over $k$ by base change, so choose finitely many algebra generators $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ for $C$. If $\mathfrak q$ represents $y$, the affine stalk localization theorem gives $C_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,y}=F$.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation); Schemes Tag 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); Algebra Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), (4); Schemes affine-stalk construction.

proof.text: Let $L/k$ be any field extension. Claim (*) of Step 1, applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of Step 3, shows that $C\otimes_kL$ is reduced. Localization commutes with tensor product: $F\otimes_kL=C_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_kL$ is the localization of $C\otimes_kL$ at the images of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$. Explicitly the comparison sends $(c\otimes l)/s$ to $(c/s)\otimes l$, with inverse $(c/s)\otimes l\mapsto(c\otimes l)/s$; these formulas are multiplicative, so it is a ring isomorphism. By the localization fact of Step 1, $F\otimes_kL$ is reduced for all $L$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 04KN (lemma-geometrically-reduced-permanence), localization argument; tensor comparison from Tags 00DK and 00D2.

proof.text: If $k$ has positive characteristic, apply the geometrically reduced field-extension criterion to Step 4 to conclude that $F/k$ is separable in the nonalgebraic sense. If $k$ has characteristic zero, use characteristic-zero separability. Also $F$ is finitely generated as a field over $k$: the residue field of $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak q)$, by the fraction description of localization; as $C_{\mathfrak q}=F$ is already a field, this residue field is $F$. The images of $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ generate $C/\mathfrak q$ as a $k$-algebra and therefore generate its fraction field as a field. Applying the definition of nonalgebraic separability to the finitely generated intermediate field $F$ itself gives a separating transcendence basis $T$ of $F/k$. A finitely generated field extension has a finite transcendence basis, and all transcendence bases have the same cardinality; hence $T$ is finite. The extension $F/k(T)$ is separable algebraic and is generated as a field by the same finite tuple of images of the $c_i$. The algebraic-generators finiteness theorem makes it finite. This proves precisely the claimed finite separating transcendence basis. Together with Step 2 it is the stated ramification-one condition.
